name: Four-Week Running Support Calibration
description:
Runner-specific core, lower-leg, hip, hamstring, and mobility support layer designed to sit around the Four-Week Running Calibration bundle. The goal is clean calibration data, durability, and trunk/pelvis control without adding bodybuilding-style leg fatigue.

Companion to: four-week-running-calibration-patched. Relationship: support_layer. Window: 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-26. Rules: Running remains the priority session. Support work must not compromise easy-run feel or calibration-quality HR data. If soreness changes the next morning's run mechanics, cut support volume before cutting running. No high-volume Nordics, no hard lunges, no abdominal circus work during this calibration block. On optional LTHR-test week, drop hamstring/adductor work if the test is completed.

Intent: running-centric durability, not hypertrophy. Weekly support budget: 20-45 minutes total most weeks. Default intensity: RPE 4-6; clean form and no grinding. Highest-cost block: Hamstring/adductor/hinge support. Lowest-cost block: Mobility reset. Quality gate: No tendon pain above mild background noise No meaningful DOMS from previous support session Easy run still feels easy by talk test Running mechanics feel normal Skip or reduce if: Calves, Achilles, hamstrings, adductors, or knees feel irritated Morning run felt unusually heavy Chest-strap calibration run was invalid due to spikes/dropouts and you need a clean rerun You are within 24 hours before or after the optional LTHR test

card_templates.name: Micro-Primer for Strides
card_templates.summary: Five-to-seven-minute mechanics primer before stride or drill days.

payload.instructions: Duration target: 6 min. Use before stride/drill runs only. This is a neural/mechanical primer, not a warm-up workout. Everything should feel springy and easy. Afterward, rate: Springiness; Calf/Achilles comfort.

exercises.label: Ankle rocks
exercises.detail: Drive the knee over the toes while the heel stays down. Find ankle range without forcing it.

exercises.label: Leg swings
exercises.detail: Stay tall and let the hip move freely without twisting the trunk.

exercises.label: A-march or A-skip
exercises.detail: Tall posture, dorsiflexed foot, knee drive straight ahead. Crisp, not aggressive.

exercises.label: Pogos
exercises.detail: Short ground contact, quiet upper body, stop if Achilles or calves feel sharp.

exercises.label: Relaxed build-ups
exercises.detail: Smooth acceleration only. These are not the actual strides.

card_templates.name: Core A — Anti-Rotation
card_templates.summary: Anti-rotation, contralateral control, and trunk stiffness for running.

payload.instructions: Duration target: 15 min. This is the main runner-core session. Keep ribs down, pelvis quiet, and breathing controlled. The goal is resisting unwanted motion, not chasing ab burn. Afterward, rate: Trunk control; Expected next-day leg freshness.

exercises.label: Pallof press
exercises.detail: Press out, hold 2s, return slowly. Hips and ribs stay square.

exercises.label: Dead bug
exercises.detail: Low back stays pressed down. Move opposite arm and leg without rib flare.

exercises.label: Suitcase carry
exercises.detail: Walk tall and resist side bend. The weight should challenge posture, not grip survival.

exercises.label: Plank shoulder taps
exercises.detail: Feet wider if needed. Tap slowly without hip sway.

card_templates.name: Core B — Lateral Chain
card_templates.summary: Side-plank, adductor, and hip-stability work for pelvis control.

payload.instructions: Duration target: 12 min. This is pelvis-control work. It should feel stable and precise. Use regressions before you let the pelvis collapse. Afterward, rate: Adductor comfort; Pelvis control.

exercises.label: Side plank
exercises.detail: Straight line from shoulder to ankle. Do not rotate open or sag.

exercises.label: Copenhagen plank regression
exercises.detail: Use bent knee on bench or short lever. Adductor work should be controlled, not crampy.

exercises.label: Single-leg glute bridge
exercises.detail: Drive through heel, full hip extension, no pelvis twist.

exercises.label: Bird dog or bear plank hold
exercises.detail: Choose bird dog if tired; bear plank if fresh. Keep pelvis quiet.

card_templates.name: Lower-Leg Support
card_templates.summary: Calf, soleus, tibialis, and foot-intrinsic durability for daily running.

payload.instructions: Duration target: 14 min. This is high-value support for daily running. Use full range and slow tempo. Stop short of calf pump that changes tomorrow's run. Afterward, rate: Achilles status after block; Foot control.

exercises.label: Straight-leg calf raise
exercises.detail: Full range. Pause at top and bottom. Add load only if bodyweight feels too easy and Achilles feels normal.

exercises.label: Bent-knee soleus raise
exercises.detail: Knees bent, controlled tempo. This is runner-relevant; do not bounce.

exercises.label: Tibialis raise
exercises.detail: Lift toes toward shins without rushing. Quality over burn.

exercises.label: Short foot + single-leg balance
exercises.detail: Create arch tension without curling toes. Eyes open unless balance is easy.

card_templates.name: Hamstring / Adductor / Hinge Support
card_templates.summary: Low-dose hinge, hamstring, adductor, and knee-drive resilience.

payload.instructions: Duration target: 14 min. This is the highest-cost support block. It is capped at one exposure per week, and zero during LTHR-test week if the test is done. The goal is resilience, not soreness. Afterward, rate: Hamstring soreness risk; Adductor soreness risk.

exercises.label: Single-leg RDL
exercises.detail: Light dumbbells or bodyweight. Hips square, soft knee, slow hinge. Balance is part of the exercise.

exercises.label: Hamstring slider curl or easy Nordic regression
exercises.detail: Choose sliders unless you already tolerate Nordics well. Slow eccentric, hands assist as needed.

exercises.label: Adductor squeeze
exercises.detail: Ball, yoga block, or Copenhagen-lite squeeze. Controlled 2s squeeze, no cramping.

exercises.label: Banded knee drives
exercises.detail: Fast but clean knee drive. Stay tall and avoid leaning back.

card_templates.name: Mobility Reset
card_templates.summary: Low-cost mobility and tissue check for recovery days.

payload.instructions: Duration target: 8 min. Use this on recovery/review days or when support work would be too much. This should make tomorrow feel better, not impress anyone. Afterward, rate: Recovery state; Tendon noise.

exercises.label: 90/90 breathing
exercises.detail: Feet on wall or bench. Exhale fully and let ribs come down.

exercises.label: Hip flexor rock-back or couch stretch
exercises.detail: Gentle. Do not crank lumbar extension.

exercises.label: Calf wall mobilization
exercises.detail: Knee tracks over toes with heel down.

exercises.label: Adductor rock-back
exercises.detail: Move slowly and stop before pinching.

exercises.label: Easy nasal walk or shakeout
exercises.detail: Only if it helps you downshift.

card_templates.name: Support Weekly Review
card_templates.summary: Weekly review of whether support work helped or contaminated running calibration.

payload.instructions: The review question is brutally simple: did support work make running smoother, unchanged, or worse?

items.label: Which support session made running feel better?
Which support session caused soreness, tendon noise, or weird mechanics?
Next week: keep, cut, or move any support block?
Did support work contaminate HR/RPE calibration data?

prescription_override_json.title: Micro-primer before first stride day
prescription_override_json.instructions: Use only if the running bundle has strides today. Keep it crisp and non-fatiguing.
prescription_override_json.adjustment: Skip pogos if calves or Achilles feel reactive.

prescription_override_json.title: Core A — first anti-rotation exposure
prescription_override_json.instructions: Easy baseline dose. This should not affect tomorrow's easy-only calibration run.

prescription_override_json.title: Lower-leg support — light baseline
prescription_override_json.instructions: Do this after the easy-only calibration run, not before. Keep calf work controlled and stop before a pump.

exercises.label: Straight-leg calf raise
exercises.detail: Bodyweight or light load, full range.

prescription_override_json.title: Core B — lateral-chain baseline
prescription_override_json.instructions: Short pelvis-control dose. Regress Copenhagen immediately if adductors cramp.

prescription_override_json.title: Recovery mobility + Week 1 support review
prescription_override_json.instructions: Mobility only. Do not add strength work today.

prescription_override_json.title: Week 1 support review
prescription_override_json.instructions: Decide whether any support work contaminated the calibration baseline.

prescription_override_json.title: Core A — normal dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Progress only by control, not load. This should still feel like support, not a workout.

exercises.label: Pallof press
exercises.detail: Same load unless Day 3 was trivial.

exercises.label: Suitcase carry
exercises.detail: Slightly heavier only if posture stays clean.

exercises.label: Plank shoulder taps
exercises.detail: Reduce stance width only if stable.

prescription_override_json.title: Micro-primer before strides
prescription_override_json.instructions: Use this before the stride run. Keep pogos elastic, not fatiguing.

prescription_override_json.title: Lower-leg support — normal dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Do after the run, separated by several hours if possible.

exercises.label: Straight-leg calf raise
exercises.detail: Add light dumbbells only if Achilles feels perfect.

prescription_override_json.title: Core B — optional after steady-aerobic check
prescription_override_json.instructions: Do this only if the steady-aerobic run felt controlled. If the run created fatigue, skip.

exercises.label: Bird dog or bear plank hold
exercises.detail: Bird dog if tired; bear plank if fresh.

prescription_override_json.title: Hamstring/adductor support — first exposure
prescription_override_json.instructions: Highest-cost block. Keep it deliberately underwhelming.

exercises.label: Hamstring slider curl
exercises.detail: Use sliders over Nordics for first exposure.

prescription_override_json.soreness_rule: If hamstrings/adductors are sore the next morning, cut this block in half next exposure.

prescription_override_json.title: Recovery mobility + Week 2 support review
prescription_override_json.instructions: Mobility only. Use the review to decide whether hamstring/adductor work stays.

prescription_override_json.title: Week 2 support review
prescription_override_json.instructions: Main decision: did the first hamstring/adductor block help, do nothing, or create bad soreness?

prescription_override_json.title: Core A — pre-test week dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Keep the session normal but not progressive. Do not chase load this week.

prescription_override_json.title: Micro-primer before strides
prescription_override_json.instructions: Keep this especially light because the optional LTHR test is coming.
prescription_override_json.adjustment: Skip pogos if calves are not fresh.

prescription_override_json.title: Lower-leg support — reduced pre-test dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Reduced volume to avoid calf/Achilles noise before LTHR test.

prescription_override_json.title: Post-LTHR-test mobility only
prescription_override_json.instructions: If you completed the diagnostic LTHR test, do mobility only. No core, no calf work, no hamstrings.

conditional_adjustment.if_lthr_test_skipped: Still keep this light; you can do Core B on Day 21.

prescription_override_json.title: Post-test recovery reset
prescription_override_json.instructions: Use this instead of drills/support if legs feel flat after the LTHR test.

prescription_override_json.title: Core B — light or skipped
prescription_override_json.instructions: Do this only if you feel fresh. If the LTHR test left fatigue, skip and review only.

prescription_override_json.title: Week 3 support review
prescription_override_json.instructions: Main decision: if the LTHR test was completed, did support work stay out of the way?

prescription_override_json.title: Core A — deload dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Half-volume anti-rotation. Week 4 is for absorption and review.

prescription_override_json.title: Micro-primer before light strides
prescription_override_json.instructions: Lightest primer of the block.

prescription_override_json.title: Lower-leg support — deload dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Reduced volume. Do not chase progression.

prescription_override_json.title: Hamstring/adductor support — half dose
prescription_override_json.instructions: Only do this if Week 2's version caused no bad soreness. Otherwise replace with Mobility Reset.

exercises.label: Hamstring slider curl
exercises.detail: Skip if hamstrings are not fresh.

prescription_override_json.title: Final mobility reset
prescription_override_json.instructions: Finish the block with mobility, not fatigue.

prescription_override_json.title: Week 4 final support review
prescription_override_json.instructions: Decide what survives into the next actual running block.
final_decision_prompts: Keep Core B weekly or every other week?
Lower-leg support once or twice weekly?
Did hamstring/adductor work earn a weekly slot?
Any support exercise that clearly made running worse?
